READY_SUBSET.json are selected here. Its SHA256 is

historical; no runtime kill, blanket equivalence or criterion change is granted.
Carry the sourced R7 derivation/retired dispositions, RV23-M5c/M7 equivalence and
optional RV23C-N1 qualification. They are not newly waived required mutants.

Existing I22 through manager may prepare for at most 10 minutes now, source-only:
- Freeze a runtime manifest in READY_SUBSET order with source/test/lock hashes,
  exact filters and qualifying semantic assertions from the reviewed inventory.
- Identical complete pre/post file bindings AND identical filter lists may share
  one physical experiment, preserving every registration as an explicit alias.
  ROOT's equality check gives 54 physical experiments for 66 registrations and
  28 distinct baseline filters. No merely similar faults may be combined.
- Prepare independent immutable FK archives under scratch/i22/protected_g1,
  one per physical experiment, plus targets under a1-protected-target/g1.
  Reuse the read-only E1 baseline and its bound binary only after source/test/
  lock/binary/fingerprint checks. No original archives or targets are pruned.
- Existing /usr/bin/patch is available. Use ordinary exact-context application
  (for example -p1 -F0 -t -i), with pre/post hashes for every affected file.
  No new mutation framework, host tool, supervisor or repair loop is authorized.

NO RUST until ROOT releases the host slot after its current FK suite. Manager
must first verify resolved containment, no symlinks/hardlinks/maintained aliases,
frozen original-byte equality and exact target paths, then report readiness.
After ROOT release, runtime is bounded to 60 minutes with a five-minute command
checkpoint. Return incomplete work at the boundary; no automatic extension.

Run the 28 distinct exact filters on the unmodified bound baseline first.
Each must select exactly one test and pass. Apply one frozen patch per owned
copy; run its exact filter with normal cleared environment and existing guard:
installed 1.97.1, auto-install0, offline/locked -j4, incremental0, testthreads2,
FK_SEEDED_FAULT/Rust flags/wrappers unset. One Cargo/process sequence at a time.
Every physical experiment requires its untouched-baseline return control.
Thus the frozen complete plan is 28 baseline +54 mutant +54 return invocations,
before any stop. Source-equivalent aliases share that same recorded result.

Credit only the reviewed named semantic assertion. In particular M24/D15 must
lose the specifically required combination R7 verdict; D4u must reach the
underflow assertion after intact overflow controls. A certificate failure,
compile failure, generic unwrap, empty filter, snapshot/work drift unrelated
to the named fault, or surviving required fault is not a kill. Stop before
later experiments on any such result; do not change a discriminator or patch
inside this grant. Accounting faults use their specifically reviewed work
assertions. Preserve stdout/stderr, source/binary/features, commands, exit,
guard and exact assertion locus, including all failed/incomplete cases.

Write only additive A1 R/I22/protected_g1 and R/manager/protected_g1 plus owned
scratch/targets. No maintained source/tests/observations, new cases, other
registries, V-K feature runs, Git/index writes or delegation. All unselected
mappings, direct-diagnostic gaps and final merge gates remain explicit.

# RV29 protected replay preparation review and queued runtime backcheck

**66 named variants are source-ready for a separately granted focused baseline/
compile/mutation run. No current kill or final A1 acceptance is claimed.**
READY_SUBSET.json gives exact group/ID, patch SHA256 and filters. The first25
cover the priority13 R7/K4 faults,11 original A2 reconstructions and D4u.
Remainder review adds14 direct R7/K4 maps and27 active RV23-family variants.
Mechanical validity of another patch does not place it in this semantic-ready
subset. COMPLETE_DISPOSITION_INDEX.json preserves all142 source/control entries
and records the unapproved/qualified boundary. V-K15/NONE/unknown remain separate.

## Exact patch review and priority results

Verified the supplied I23 seal026823c7ad17e0415f679c37ef5dd854a05086e963e82c2aa3bd752b083e497e
and additive seal. Independently applied all136 unified patches **in memory** to
frozen40129 source. Every context/preimage and declared postimage hash matches;
none edits a protected test. No source file, patch or diagnostic was authored,
applied on disk or run by RV29. Source mechanics alone are not semantic kills.

The17 stale R7/K4 mappings now use the actual producer sites: shared relative_class,
current A2-wrapped bound operations, separate shift_start/certificates, precise
attempt/verification charge sites, and the first assembled entry assignment
before seeded hooks. R7-M8 updates both floor scaling constants and preserves
public visibility. R7-M26/M24 choose their estimator surrogate in the existing
Result-returning verifier context; R7-M29 retains original per-block bound
metadata after using global Uc and body scope. These implement the named faults;
R7-M24 remains a derivation disposition, not a kill requirement.

K4-M24 and D15 correctly alter the old verdict and leave the genuine new
certificate active. Neither fabricates a CertifiedPublication or calls obsolete
finish_selected arguments. Their existing structured verdict test can discriminate
them: every_control_follows_gens_schedule_and_r7s_expectations_honestly first
compares each named model's exact selected/token tuple to GEN, then explicitly
pins CEIL5A3's operands at512 and its combination's128 Pivot /256 estimate /512
StopRule rejections. K4-M24 overwrites the tied512 rejection; D15 also overwrites
256. A later genuine certificate cannot restore those old R7 verdict tokens.
Credit only the named combination's missing required R7 verdict or explicitly
pinned unwarranted acceptance. Mere Ceiling, a generic certificate error or
unrelated earlier failure supplies no kill. Use the existing full filter first;
no new oracle or focused extraction is required unless runtime shows that the
relevant assertion cannot be reached.

All11 original A2 patches preserve their specific meanings, separately from
review variants: unavailable-as-zero, min/max, refusal stop, each of four stopped
stage closures, block isolation, Budget/refusal classification, no-data handling
and refusal alternatives. Original I19 bytes remain unrecovered; these are
explicit current reconstructions, not fabricated historical byte matches.
The min/max filter reaches its both-available scalar assertion; M6 reaches the
direct Budget/Exponent refusable checks; M8's expected Ok(bounds) versus the
introduced Span at that exact uc_bounds call is its intended semantic outcome.

D4u is an assertion-preserving current underflow diagnostic. It uses verifier
membership only when candidate or verifier is Underflow. Both original overflow
assertions remain and retain candidate membership; the first original underflow
straddle assertion must fail at StopRule index1 versus None. This source-qualified
variant is accepted for that finite semantic experiment, not as the original
assertion-deleting bytes. Ordinary D4 and all historical records remain registered.

## Additional matching maps and concrete gaps

Fourteen additional R7/K4 maps have direct scalar/prepublication checks: R7-M1,
M2, M6, M10, M11, M16, M18, M20, M22, M23; K4-M6, M10, M14a and M14b. Their
required errors are named equation, precision, geometry, bound, netting or rule-
order observations rather than record drift. The27 active RV23-family bodies
retain their source-qualified refusal/stage/precedence effects. For RV23-M6,
the proposed filter's initial completed-run assertion at kf3_tests.rs547 checks
the missing refusal before its budget loop. For RV23-M6b, READY_SUBSET routes to
the existing direct refusable Exponent-slot assertion, avoiding reliance on a
possible downstream generic unwrap panic. Neither filter proves cached
non-budget replay; the optional qualification below is separate.

**P06-1 — R7-M5 mapping remains open.** Its patch changes verify_state's E input
for prescribed DOFs. The proposed e_charge... filter checks residual/W/a_s/charge/
W_plus digests and later ratios, but does not directly assert r.e_rows against
accepted E rows. A relevant ratio assertion may discriminate; the advertised
per-row E assertion is not present there. Identify the actual intended existing
assertion or compare that verifier's r.e_rows/resolution to the fixed SCALE
corpus in a minimal separately reviewed diagnostic. Do not compute expected E
by calling the same production path. No production bug or retirement is claimed.

R7-M13 and K4-M11/M12/M13/M15 were inspected but are outside this ready subset:
their proposed tests require selection/publication before the intended residual,
formation or coupled-scale assertion. If a certificate rejects first, that
precondition failure is not their numerical/evidence kill. A finite future run
may demonstrate that the existing assertion remains reachable; otherwise reuse
its unchanged expectation at the appropriate earlier seam. This is a mapping
qualification, not permission to alter protected expectations.

I23's existing R7-M12, K4-M37, D2 and D10 discriminator gaps remain. Other
ordinary patches not specifically included in READY_SUBSET received mechanical
checking only in this bounded review and remain unapproved for semantic credit.
No blanket retirement or arbitrary-failure acceptance is proposed.

## Additive diagnostic proposals

The five proposed test functions plus report helper address seven entries:
R7-M3/M4/M9 (floor precision), M25 (data/g scope), M26 (B choice), M28 (required
shift), M29 (compound scope/bound/shift). The calls occur before publication and
use existing fixtures. Their [true,false] flags, zero-data theta and g limits,
and required shift counts match the fixed charge.txt records inspected here.
B choice is re-expressed as min over formed Uc/S rather than calling certified
to compute its own expected result. This is a reasonable finite proposal for
separate installation/compilation/baseline validation; it is not runtime-ready
merely because its text applies, and no diagnostic was installed here.

Keep the floor/scope/bound labels as the qualifying assertions. An earlier
compile, unwrap or certificate error does not establish those checks. Do not
apply the proposed B-choice diagnostic to redefine R7-M24 as a required kill.
The historical guards/derivations R7-M17/M21/M24/M27, derived M14 and retired
M19 remain exactly their sourced dispositions; R7-M27's low-precision stress
obligation remains distinct from its design-precision survivor status.
